title: “I hurt all of you”: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff and says the company doesn’t need a succession plan
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang struck a conciliatory and remorseful tone on Tuesday as he led his first employee meeting since being reinstated, telling staff he let them down and promising to do a better job the second time around, CNBC reported on November 24, 2026, citing people inside the room. “I hurt all of you,” Huang said, according to one of the people. He told employees Nvidia has built a team that doesn’t require succession planning the way a normal organization does, because multiple capable leaders run different parts of the company, and said a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy. Huang opened by thanking CFO Colette Kress for her leadership as interim CEO, called the gathering the second hardest meeting of his life, the first being with his wife, and said he is in therapy. He resigned on Nov. 12 after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing, and was reinstated by the board on Monday. The stock surged more than 30% the day his return was announced, then fell on Tuesday.

title: Trump says a pardon for Jensen Huang is “always an option” and floats a U.S. stake in Nvidia
summary: President Donald Trump said he would be willing to pardon reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if needed after Huang appears before Congress next week, according to an exclusive New York Post interview reported by CNBC on November 25, 2026. Trump said a pardon was “always an option” but that he did not think it would be “necessary,” and that Huang should not need to invoke the Fifth Amendment when he appears for a closed-door interview with the House Foreign Affairs Committee on Dec. 1 and before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3. “I think I want him to just tell the truth,” Trump said. He also said he was open to the U.S. government taking an equity stake in Nvidia, similar to its 2025 stake in Intel. Nvidia shares surged 31% on Monday after Huang’s reinstatement before falling 5.9% on Tuesday amid a broader market pullback. Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said he expected Huang to take the Fifth, while Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., called the whole thing “a money-making operation.” At Tuesday’s all-hands, Huang told staff, “We are the most apolitical company.”

title: U.S. jury convicts Huawei of fraud, sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets
summary: Chinese technology giant Huawei was convicted on Tuesday in New York on multiple federal criminal charges, including fraud, U.S. sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, after a three-month trial, CNBC reported on November 25, 2026, citing the Justice Department. A federal jury found Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty of offenses including bank and wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The department said Huawei misrepresented its activities in Iran to banks to secure billions of dollars and supplied surveillance cameras that enabled Iranian authorities to monitor protests. Prosecutors said Huawei copied source code used in Cisco routers, with engineers spelling Cisco’s name backward to conceal it, and that employees sent photographs and details of T-Mobile’s touchscreen-testing robot to China, with one removing a component from T-Mobile’s lab in a backpack. “No person or company is above the law,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. Huawei welcomed its acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge and said the remaining charges are “equally without legal or factual merit.” Sentencing is scheduled for Sept. 14, 2027.

title: Meta brings its Muse AI agent straight into Instagram DMs
summary: Instagram users can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the company announced on Tuesday, TechCrunch reported on November 24, 2026. Users can ask Muse for more context about a post, place or product, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs, without toggling over to the Muse app. They can share posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to a Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes; those chats appear as a side chat in the main Muse app. The DM feature began rolling out Tuesday on iOS and Android in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan and Singapore. Muse can also organize saved posts and reels into Collections, turn a recipe video into a grocery list or build a trip itinerary from travel creators’ content; that saved-post prompt is launching in the U.S. and Canada. Meta says nothing is shared, published or sent without users’ approval, and they can ask Muse to forget information or undo actions at any time.

title: Tidal will ban fully AI-generated songs and delete more than 29 million tracks by year’s end
summary: Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI, TechCrunch reported on November 24, 2026. Over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to Tidal were AI-generated, the company said. It will begin removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, a process that will delete more than 29 million songs by the end of the year, and expects to reject roughly 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day under the new rules. Distributors are barred from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and submissions whose metadata says they were made fully with AI will be rejected, though songs made with AI assistance are still accepted. Tidal said 27 million tracks, or 6.3% of its catalog, are fully AI-generated, and 96% of those have no streams. “At this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried,” the company said. TechCrunch noted Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright; Tidal had started de-monetizing AI songs in June.

title: S&P 500 futures fall 2% and Nasdaq-100 futures slump 3% as the AI sell-off returns
summary: U.S. stock futures tumbled on Wednesday, November 25, as the artificial intelligence trade faced more pressure and traders weighed the prospect of more U.S. tariffs, CNBC reported in its live markets coverage. Nasdaq-100 futures slumped 3%, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures dropped 682 points, or 1.4%, and S&P 500 futures fell 2%. Nvidia slid more than 5% in the premarket and Anthropic dropped 4%, while Oracle declined about 5% and Alphabet shed 3%. Wall Street was coming off a losing session on Tuesday: the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq slid 1.5%, while the Dow climbed more than 400 points, or 0.9%. Economists polled by Dow Jones expected October’s PCE price index to rise 0.3% for the month and 3.8% annually, and weekly jobless claims arrived a day early because U.S. markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. “Let’s remember that the sell-off in the AI ecosystem predated the news about Huang and Nvidia,” Schwab’s Liz Ann Sonders told CNBC.

title: Nvidia gives back 6.86% to $153.73 a day after its 31% surge, as Micron drops 10.6%
summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.53% to 23,720.88 at 1:51 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 24, as semiconductor and AI stocks gave back a day-old rally, Chip Dispatch reported. Nvidia traded at $153.73, down 6.86%, or $11.32, one session after surging 31% on Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO. The S&P 500 sat at 7,197.07, down 0.55%, while the Dow rose 0.75% to 49,967.97. The sell-off ran deeper than Nvidia, per CNBC quote data cited by Chip Dispatch: CoreWeave fell 12.4% to $42.34, Dell 11.4% to $296.61, Micron 10.6% to $632.53, AMD 8.9% to $413.30 and Intel 7.6% to $55.12, while the VanEck Semiconductor ETF dropped 6.9%. Anthropic fell 8.57% to $80.13, below its $83 IPO price. Retail earnings carried the Dow, with Abercrombie & Fitch up 24.2% and DICK’S Sporting Goods up 17%.

title: SoftBank sheds 14.83% as the global tech rout deepens and Asian chip stocks reverse
summary: Technology stocks tumbled globally on Wednesday, November 25, as renewed concerns over the AI trade rattled investors and Monday’s rally faded, CNBC reported. Technology-focused investor SoftBank Group shed 14.83% in Tokyo. Advantest, a supplier of chip-testing equipment to Nvidia, plunged 12.94%, Tokyo Electron slumped 12.53% and Lasertec lost 11.23%. In South Korea, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plunged 9.87% and 11.05%, respectively, and in Taiwan, TSMC tumbled 3.59% while Hon Hai Precision Industry fell 8.83%. Nvidia was down 4.65% in premarket trading at 4:11 a.m. ET. Futurum Group analyst Rolf Bulk said the renewed sell-off largely reflects lingering concerns over the sustainability of AI spending beyond 2027. Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid said “it’s pretty wild out there,” but added that “we’re back to the rotation trade rather than the indiscriminate sell-off” of late last week.

title: Dell crushes estimates on AI server demand and authorizes a $25 billion buyback
summary: Dell reported third-quarter results on Tuesday, November 24, that topped Wall Street expectations and gave a strong fourth-quarter outlook, CNBC reported. Adjusted earnings were $9.45 a share versus $6.59 expected, and revenue was $54.94 billion versus $49.32 billion, per LSEG. Overall sales more than doubled year over year, driven by AI server demand. The infrastructure solutions group posted $41.97 billion in sales, including $22 billion for AI-optimized servers, up 291%, and now accounts for 85% of revenue. Dell guided to $8.40 a share on about $56.3 billion in revenue this quarter, raised its next-fiscal-year AI server forecast to $78 billion and cited a $132.3 billion AI server backlog. “We are now a different company,” vice chairman and COO Jeff Clarke said. PC and laptop sales of $12.89 billion missed estimates. Dell authorized $25 billion in share repurchases; its shares rose in extended trading and are up over 135% in 2026, though CNBC’s Wednesday premarket coverage reported Dell falling despite the beat.

title: Baidu opens Apache 2.0 weights for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, a 280B mixture-of-experts model
summary: Baidu has made ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview weights publicly available through its Hugging Face repositories, Open Model Weights reported on November 24, 2026, fulfilling the weight-release commitment in the earlier Preview announcement that first offered the model through Baidu’s hosted platform. The model card describes a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture with 280 billion total parameters and 14 billion active per token, plus a reported context window of one million tokens. The default checkpoint combines blockwise FP8 with FP4 experts and includes a DSpark draft head for speculative decoding, and Baidu also lists FP8 and BF16 variants. The Preview repository declares Apache 2.0. Open Model Weights called it an important release for self-hosted professional AI and long-context research, but cautioned that a low active-parameter count doesn’t mean small-model storage needs, that the model remains a preview, and that reported capabilities are publisher claims, not independently reproduced results.

title: Sarvam AI releases Sarvam-105B-1711, with a 65 GB version that runs on a single workstation GPU
summary: Sarvam AI has announced Sarvam-105B-1711, an updated checkpoint for high-volume applications such as conversational assistants, voice-agent pipelines and tool-enabled workflows, Open Model Weights reported on November 24, 2026. The developer’s November 22 announcement describes it as an improvement over the earlier Sarvam 105B, and it links both NVFP4 and BF16 weight repositories, with Apache 2.0 declared on their model cards. Sarvam describes the NVFP4 version as about 65 GB and reports it can run on a single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell workstation GPU under the company’s serving configuration. The company emphasizes instruction following, tool execution and Indian-language conversation, including users who switch languages mid-conversation, and reports improved results on its conversational evaluation suite. Open Model Weights said the release adds to the geographic and linguistic diversity of downloadable models, but noted it has not independently reproduced the benchmarks and that long contexts and serving stacks change real memory needs.

title: PrismML’s Ternary Bonsai 2.5 squeezes a 27B coding agent into 5.9 GB
summary: PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B on Tuesday, November 24, a coding agent model that occupies 5.9 GB of memory, roughly nine times less than the 54 GB the same 27-billion-parameter model would need at 16-bit precision, Chip Dispatch reported on November 25, 2026. The Caltech-spawned startup published the weights on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0. Built on Qwen3.8 27B, the ternary model restricts every weight to minus one, zero or plus one. On SWE-bench Verified it scores 75.6, up from 60.8 for Bonsai 2, versus 80.6 for the full-precision base model, and its AppWorld score rose to 90.5 from 51.2, all according to PrismML and not independently reproduced. It runs via llama.cpp on Nvidia and Intel GPUs and MLX on Apple devices, with throughput of 204 tokens per second on an RTX 4090 and 291 on an H100 using multi-token prediction. “Small errors can compound across successive tool calls and derail an entire task,” the company wrote.

title: Uber and Nuro pull the safety drivers and start driverless tests of Lucid Gravity robotaxis
summary: Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area, more than six months after receiving the permit that allowed them to remove the human safety driver, TechCrunch reported on November 24, 2026. The companies will soon begin offering driverless rides to employees in the final lead-up to launching a commercial robotaxi service in the first quarter of 2027. Uber’s planned investment in Lucid has grown from $300 million to $500 million, and it agreed to buy at least 35,000 Lucid Gravity SUVs, up from 20,000. The California DMV granted Nuro a driverless permit in May 2026, and the companies are also testing in Houston with safety operators. Their combined engineering fleet, which stood at 100 vehicles earlier this year, is expanding as Lucid begins manufacturing the first production robotaxis at its Arizona factory. The Gravity robotaxi carries high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar and radar, while Uber, which will own and operate the fleet, focuses on the in-cabin experience.

title: Fluidstack launches Blackbird, a factory-built data center that scales to 400 MW in six months
summary: Fluidstack launched Blackbird on November 25, a modular data-center platform it says can scale from a single zone of more than 10 MW to a 400 MW facility and be completed within six months of groundbreaking, compared with an industry build time of 18 to 24 months, Chip Dispatch reported. Modules are fabricated off site, shipped as integrated and tested units and assembled at the campus, an approach Fluidstack expects to cut build times by two-thirds or more. The platform includes a Compute Module, a self-supporting overhead structure carrying power, cooling and cabling that works with standard racks and any chip, and an Electrical Skid that accepts a 35 kV-class supply and delivers 480 V or 415 V. All three products are built at a Glendale, Arizona plant larger than 1.1 million square feet with 1,250 permanent jobs. “Fluidstack engineers and designs data centers in the U.S., then assembles them on construction sites across the country,” CEO Gary Wu said. Chip Dispatch noted no Blackbird customer or site was named and the 400 MW figure is a maximum stated scale.

title: Jülich orders a 200-qubit silicon quantum computer from ARQUE Systems for about €35 million
summary: Forschungszentrum Jülich will receive a semiconductor-based quantum computer with up to 200 qubits by the end of 2029, built by ARQUE Systems under a project worth roughly 35 million euros, Chip Dispatch reported on November 25, 2026. The contract, announced Wednesday, pairs the Jülich spin-off with its parent research center on a machine that will join JUNIQ, the center’s quantum computing user facility. ARQUE’s qubits are the spins of single electrons trapped in silicon and silicon-germanium structures, and a patent-pending shuttling method moves those electrons across the chip so each qubit doesn’t need its own control line. ARQUE projects the approach could eventually fit more than ten million qubits on a chip of about 2 by 2 centimeters, a company projection; the machine it already integrated into JUNIQ runs five qubits. Ninety percent of the funding comes from Germany’s Coal Regions Investment Act and North Rhine-Westphalia pays the rest. “A sovereign Europe needs technological strength,” said state economy minister Mona Neubaur.

title: A boy’s promise to his mother became Thanksgiving Heroes, now feeding thousands of families
summary: What began as an 11-year-old boy’s promise to his mother has become Thanksgiving Heroes, a nationwide effort to bring holiday meals to families in need, Good News Network reported on November 24, 2026. Founder Rob Adams grew up the oldest of six children in South Texas, and for a stretch his family lived out of their pickup truck. One Christmas, a neighboring family, the Christiansons, let the Adamses stay in their home while they were away, leaving the refrigerator stocked with turkey and pumpkin pie and presents under the tree. Adams told his mother he would pay it forward one day, and years later, as she faced a brain-cancer diagnosis, she urged him to follow through. His first-year goal was 10 families; the group fed about 755. This year it aims to reach 3,600 families across Utah, and its network of affiliates has served more than 29,000 families. Volunteers deliver meal kits with a turkey and sides to families nominated by neighbors, and no one has to prove need. “The opportunity is right there,” Adams said.

title: 33 kids wrote to a wounded Vietnam corpsman in 1967. Now his son is finding them to say thank you
summary: In 1967, 33 schoolchildren at St. Ann School in Gloucester, Massachusetts, wrote letters to a Navy corpsman they had never met, and almost 60 years later his son is tracking them down to thank them, Good News Network reported on November 23, 2026. HM3 Russell Jacobson had suffered 12 gunshot wounds and grenade shrapnel in Vietnam and lay in a full-body cast at Chelsea Naval Hospital, non-verbal for weeks and down to about 80 pounds. A nurse’s sister, a nun at the school, had the children write. One boy wrote about his pet lizard; another asked about the Montreal Expos. As the nurse recalled, when Russell began reading the letters he started getting back on his feet. “It was the most genuine thing ever,” his son Dave Jacobson told GNN. Dave has so far connected with 18 of the 33 letter writers, starting with the nun who organized the project, now 90. “These little acts they thought would never be brought up again, you know, they made a difference,” he said.

title: A retired math teacher turns broken guitars and a violin into a bird café on Prince Edward Island
summary: A retired teacher on Prince Edward Island is giving scrapped musical instruments a second life as bird feeders, Good News Network reported on November 24, 2026. Former math teacher Rob Burke runs what he calls the Frets and Feathers Cafe after seeing someone in Europe turn an old guitar into a feeder on social media and deciding to do one better with a whole orchestra. He asked on Facebook for broken instruments for an art project and received six guitars, an old violin and pieces of a drum set, then attached driftwood perches and metal feeding dishes to the hollow-body guitars. His glue gun worked at first, CBC reported, but once heavier blue jays began visiting he had to reattach the perches more firmly. Burke has since spotted a woodpecker, corvids and chickadees and expects more species as the seasons change, and he welcomes more instrument donations from fellow Islanders to expand his “Peck and Play Orchestra.”

title: Family Storytime with chicken stories at the East Regional Library this morning
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s East Regional Library hosts Family Storytime on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, from 9:30 to 10:30 a.m. in the Story Time Room, according to the library’s event calendar. The listing invites families to “begin your child’s literacy education with a star-studded lineup of stories, music, fingerplays, and other activities,” and says the program is designed to be inclusive of all ages and families. This week’s books are Chicken Story Time by Sandy Asher, Chickens to the Rescue by John Himmelman and Blue Chicken by Deborah Freedman. Questions can go to (337) 445-3168. The library’s website notes that all locations close at 6 p.m. today and stay closed through Sunday, November 29, for Thanksgiving.

title: Makerspace Open Access at the Main Library this afternoon
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Main Library opens its Maker Space / Tech Lab on the third floor for Makerspace Open Access on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, from 1 to 5:30 p.m., according to the library’s event calendar. The listing says open access time lets patrons “explore and experiment as they independently work on projects of their choosing,” with self-guided online tutorials available for most applications. It is open to all ages, and no registration is required. The library system closes at 6 p.m. today and remains closed through Sunday, November 29; the calendar lists the next Makerspace open access session for Tuesday, December 1.

title: Free Yoga in the Park at Moncus Park’s First Horizon Amphitheater tonight
summary: Moncus Park hosts its free Yoga in the Park session on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, from 6 to 7 p.m., part of the “Fit For All” series presented by Louisiana Orthopaedic Specialists & Orthopedic Urgent Care, according to the park’s event listing and calendar. The class meets at the First Horizon Amphitheater unless otherwise noted, and the instructor schedule lists Allie Edge for Nov. 25. All ages and experience levels are welcome, no registration is required, and participants should bring their own mat and water and wear comfortable clothing. The listing says class may be canceled or moved due to rain or excessive heat and to check the park’s social media stories each Wednesday for updates.

title: The 5th Annual JPJ Memorial Turkey Trot runs at Moncus Park on Thanksgiving morning
summary: The 5th Annual JPJ Memorial 1-mile Turkey Trot will be held at 9 a.m. on Thanksgiving morning, Thursday, November 26, 2026, at Moncus Park, according to the park’s event listing, which shows it from 9 to 11 a.m. on its calendar. The externally hosted event, produced by JPJ Memorial, honors Jean Paul Judice, who “knew that every person mattered and he loved them unconditionally.” This year the race is raising funds for St. Joseph Diner, which has served meals to people experiencing hunger and food insecurity since 1983. “This race is the perfect setting to come together to show gratitude with your community,” the listing says. Registration is through the JPJ Memorial Turkey Trot link on the page.
